source_snapshot.procedure: Create four-member mdadm [0|1|5], format/mount/copy/hash, fail/remove/re-add one member, monitor rebuild, verify hash and tear down.
source_snapshot.criteria: Create, fault, remove, add and rebuild successfully with correct file hash and array state.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL only polls guessed /dev/md5 and does not create, degrade or prove the source lifecycle.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires RAID5 confirmation, four disposable members, exact fault/replacement identity, degraded availability, rebuild progress and cleanup.

old_problem: The Rebuild RAID5 identity coexisted with a generic level placeholder, while DeepSeek's guessed monitor-only /dev/md5 loop could not prove the intended fault, degraded data availability, rebuild or final integrity.
disposition_reason: The row title fixes RAID5 and the Procedure explicitly defines a valid four-member /dev/md3 lifecycle. Exact members and the single fault/replacement identity are runtime parameters. Coverage requires the real create-to-degraded-to-rebuilding-to-clean transition, not a clean-status polling shortcut.
decision_basis: Directly read Compatibility row133 all18 XLSX cells and history2740.
Resolved level=5 from the row identity while preserving four members, /dev/md3 role, filesystem/hash and teardown.
Required one verified fault and observed rebuild progression; rejected guessed /dev/md5 monitoring-only evidence. No DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Parameterized four-member mdadm RAID5 rebuild-transition validation
test_case.purpose: Verify an approved disposable four-member NVMe RAID5 remains data-available after one exact member fault/removal, visibly rebuilds that member after re-add, returns clean and preserves the 512 MiB file hash.
required_package: Four disposable NVMe stable identities plus the exact single fault/re-add member
Critical destructive authorization with OS/mount/swap/LVM/RAID/data exclusions
Approved file/hash, mount path, rebuild timeout, load/thermal/health thresholds
OOB access, one-fault-only guard, teardown and recovery plan
test_case.test_command: After stable exclusions and approval, build the exact four-member level=5 /dev/md3, verify clean state, create/mount ext4 and record the 512 MiB file hash. Fail/remove exactly the approved member, prove degraded availability and hash, re-add it, capture timestamped mdadm progress from spare rebuilding to active sync/clean, recheck hash, then perform approved targeted teardown.
test_case.expected_result: The intended member alone transitions active to faulty/removed to rebuilding to active sync; the array remains available while degraded, rebuild progresses to clean within approved limits, file hashes match, and cleanup touches only the four members.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires evidence of every named state transition, degraded data availability, nonzero observed rebuild progress, clean completion and matching hashes. A final clean snapshot or monitor-only loop cannot pass.
safety_gate: Authorize create, mkfs, fault and metadata clearing separately within the destructive plan.
Pin all members by stable identity and exclude protected storage.
Never fault a second member or add an unverified replacement while degraded/rebuilding.
Abort on wrong member, stalled/regressing progress, hash/I/O/filesystem/media/thermal/power/BMC error or lost recovery; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Approval, topology/member/fault map and preflight exclusions
Exact create/detail clean baseline and initial file hash
Re-add output and timestamped rebuild progress samples through clean
Post-rebuild hash, health/logs and targeted teardown/final topology
test_case.recovery: If the transition deviates, stop further mutations, protect the remaining three members, preserve mdadm events/detail, hashes, process and health logs, and require storage-owner recovery. Do not force assembly, fail another member or clear superblocks while degraded/rebuilding/mounted.
